newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backeds firmer ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backeds firmer ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities (MBS) prices were firmer late Monday in slow trading ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve policy makers on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), traders said.
Discount mortgage coupons were 3/32 to 11/32 firmer, while premium coupons were 1/32 to 4/32 firmer.
The FOMC was not expected to change interest rates, but traders cited heightened volatility ahead of the meeting.
"There has been a slight increase in volatilities, partially related to the FOMC meeting," Sally Ann Runyon, senior MBS analyst at Technical Data.

Runyon noted that heightened volatility seen in equity markets has bled over into Treasuries and mortgage securities. The affect on mortgage-backed volatilities, she said, has been slight but they are up.

Among 30-year 7 1/2-percent MBS, Government National Mortgage Association bonds were up 8/32 to 101-10/32 to yield 7.32 percent, Freddie Macs gained 3/32 to 101-18/32 for a yield of 7.26 percent and Fannie Maes advanced 10/32 to 101-10/32 to yield 7.27 percent.
Meanwhile, 10-year Treasury notes rose 7/32 to 99 12/32 to yield 6.21 percent.
